correctness.rationale: From stationary symmetric Laplace displacement and no-reset renewal conditional independence, integrate the Gaussian bivariate event across negative-half-line anchors to obtain exact F(h)=(3-h²)Φ(-h)+hφ(h). Campbell total covariance yields H(t)=ρ√D/4 E[R^-1/2 F(√(2Rt))]. Mellin integral and dominated convergence give positive K_a t^-(a+1/2); a triangular variance-integral argument proves all three rates and the quenched plateau. Numerical double quadrature checks of Gaussian kernel and Mellin constants were run independently; these support but do not prove infinite-time limits.

value.rationale: A physically motivated quenched rate distribution changes a stationary current from exponentially mixing conditional components into an algebraic aggregate with exact asymptotic amplitude. The new sharp threshold a=1/2 distinguishes anomalous T^-(a+1/2), logarithmically slowed log(T)/T, and ordinary T^-1 temporal self-averaging despite each constituent having finite correlation time. This is an explicit noncommuting slow-mode/long-time limit, not a fixed-rate constant substitution.
